ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a square border, with a black shaded four-pointed curved-edge region inside; the four pointed tips respectively face the midpoints of the four sides of the square; the four corners of the square are unshaded white curved-edge regions, corresponding to the four quarter circles drawn at the respective vertices. The problem text gives that the side length of the square is 6, and the radius of each quarter circle is 3. Reasoning: According to the meaning of the problem and the figure, the shaded area is equal to the area of the entire square minus the areas of the four unshaded quarter circles. The area of the square is 6^2=36. The four quarter circles with radius 3 together equal one whole circle with radius 3, whose area is π·3^2=9π. So the shaded area is 36-9π. Comparing with a-bπ, a=36, b=9, therefore a+b=45.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: a square contains a black shaded central four-pointed region, with each side midpoint forming a sharp point of the shaded region and each corner occupied by an unshaded quarter-circle sector. Read from the text that the square has side length 6 and that each quarter-circle has radius 3. Treat the shaded area as the whole square minus the four unshaded quarter-circles at the vertices. Compute square area 6^2 = 36. The four quarter-circles together make one full circle of radius 3, area 9π. Thus shaded area = 36 - 9π, so a = 36 and b = 9, giving a + b = 45.
